raw_case_text:
A 30-year-old 54 kg female presented to us with severe pain in the right elbow and forearm following trauma to the right elbow. Signs of neurovascular compression distal to the site of injury were evident in the injured limb. She had a history of intermittent high-grade fever with chill and rigor and generalized weakness for 3 days. There was no history of any cardio-respiratory abnormality or anaphylaxis to any drug. On presentation, her Glasgow Coma Scale was 15/15 and she was found to have heart rate, blood pressure and respiratory rate of 118/min, 124/72 mmHg and 15breaths/min respectively. She was febrile and appeared anemic, and cardiovascular and respiratory system examinations were normal. Hepatosplenomegaly was evident on per abdominal examination. Her airway examination was normal. Hemogram of the patient showed hemoglobin of 6.3g/dL and total leukocyte count of 14600/cmm. Her serum electrolytes, liver function test, renal function test and random blood sugar were within normal limits. We decided to send the patient's blood sample for parasitological examination as per the clinical presentation (other than those due to trauma). In view of suspected neurovascular compression in the right upper limb a decision to explore the fracture was taken. In the operation theater routine monitors were connected followed by premedication with intravenous (IV) fentanyl (2mug/kg). The patient's trachea was intubated with a 7.5-mm poly vinyl chloride (PVC) cuffed tracheal tube following a rapid sequence induction with standard dosage of thiopentone and rocuronium. Correct placement of the tracheal tube was confirmed and GA was maintained with isoflurane, inj vecuronium and fentanyl.
The patient had a stable intraoperative course for 1 hour. Mean while, the patient was reported to have Plasmodium falciparum infection(with asexual forms of Plasmodium falciparum in the blood and a parasite count of 6300/cmm). After that we administered IV artesunate (2.4mg/kg) to the patient intraoperatively. Immediately following artesunate administration, hypotension and increased airway pressures was noticed. We suspected an anaphylactic reaction and all the anesthetic gases were discontinued. The patient's lung was ventilated with 100% oxygen followed by administration of IV epinephrine (0.2microg/kg), hydrocortisone (5mg/kg) and 2L of normal saline solution. In view of the persistent hypotension, epinephrine infusion was administered for a short duration. After 30 min, the patient's blood pressure and air way pressure returned to normal. The remaining 4h of the surgery were uneventful and the patient was shifted intubated to the intensive care unit (ICU). In the ICU, IV quinine dihydrochloride (10 mg/kg) was given over a period of 4 h to the patient, and was repeated every 8 hourly. Patient's trachea was extubated after 6 h of ICU admission. She had an uneventful ICU stay and was discharged from the ICU on the 3rd day. Before discharge, a positive intradermal skin test for artesunate was observed.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 30-year-old female presented with severe right elbow and forearm pain following trauma, accompanied by a 3-day history of intermittent high-grade fever with chills, rigors, and generalized weakness.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient sustained trauma to the right elbow resulting in severe right elbow/forearm pain and distal neurovascular compression, and concurrently reported a 3-day history of intermittent high-grade fever with chills, rigors, and generalized weakness.
subjective.past_medical_history: Weight 54 kg; no history of cardiorespiratory abnormalities or drug anaphylaxis.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for right elbow/forearm trauma pain, intermittent high-grade fever, chills, rigors, and generalized weakness. No known drug allergies prior to admission.

objective.physical_examination: GCS 15/15, febrile, clinically anemic, HR 118/min, BP 124/72 mmHg, RR 15 breaths/min, normal airway, cardiovascular, and respiratory exams, hepatosplenomegaly on abdominal palpation, and signs of distal neurovascular compression in the injured right upper limb. Intraoperatively developed acute hypotension and elevated airway pressures immediately following IV artesunate injection.
objective.routine_investigations: Hemoglobin 6.3 g/dL, total leukocyte count 14,600/cmm, and normal serum electrolytes, LFTs, renal function tests, and random blood sugar.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Right elbow fracture with neurovascular compression and concurrent Plasmodium falciparum malaria, complicated by intraoperative anaphylactic shock to intravenous artesunate. Malaria was confirmed intraoperatively by peripheral blood examination showing asexual forms of P. falciparum (parasite count 6,300/cmm), and artesunate allergy was confirmed before discharge by a positive intradermal skin test. During open fracture exploration under general anesthesia, acute anaphylaxis to IV artesunate (2.4 mg/kg) was successfully resuscitated with 100% oxygen, IV epinephrine (0.2 ug/kg bolus plus brief infusion), IV hydrocortisone (5 mg/kg), and 2 L normal saline; malaria therapy was completed in the ICU with IV quinine dihydrochloride (10 mg/kg over 4 hours q8h), and she was extubated at 6 hours and discharged from the ICU on day 3.
